author: jochembrouwer
content:
Hi all, I believe we should at least raise the min spec of 500 MB/s to at least 1 GiB/s. This would put the max read time (for these accounts targeted by EVM, so not other r/w jobs like MPT node reading/writing) on:

`(block_gas_limit // COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS * MAX_CODE_SIZE) / READ_SPEED = 4.069s` (note that with current spec this means that we take at most 8+ seconds for this block which is thus too long)

I would personally up it to 2 GiB/s as this leaves us more room (and max block time of slightly more of 2s at this 200M gas limit)

Here is one from Corsair 2021: https://ir.corsair.com/news-releases/news-release-details/blazing-fast-gen4-speeds-corsair-launches-mp600-core-and-mp600 (7100 MB/s)
Sells for 430EUR: https://www.amazon.nl/Corsair-MP600-NVMe-PCIe-Gen4/dp/B09Q2NCFS7?th=1

I think we should up it to 2 GiB/s to leave some headroom. Would love some extra advise from people with more knowledge of hardware.

author: jochembrouwer
content:
This depends on the gas limit and the max contract size. Note that we increased from 60MGas -> 200MGas and that we increased from 24 KiB to 64 Kib max size (this is a multiplication factor of almost 9! So for same max block execution time one would have to up their disk by a factor 9 read speed)

Currently, with Fusaka factors, we have can target at most 23076 accounts (`60_000_000 // 2600`(`COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCCESS_COST`, ref: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2929)) of 24 KiB, so the max (read) time of this is: `(23076 * 24 * 1024) / (500 * 1024 * 1024) = 1.0816875s`

But due to the (almost) 9x multiplication factor we thus up this to 9 seconds in Glamsterdam which is not enough

author: jochembrouwer
content: I will bring this up on ACDT, I think it makes sense to create new specs for Glamsterdam, it also makes sense that over time these specs change
